bear.narrative: A full chemical and plastics down-cycle: cheaper imports force distributors to compete on price, revenue growth halves to about two per cent a year against the base four to five, the delivered gross margin gives back two of the points won in 2026 and sits at the FY2025 trough for the whole forecast, the bond and bank lines reprice nearly a third higher at the refinancing, and the rupiah weakens five per cent against the dollar so the imported cost base runs ahead of the repricing lag. The associate book is carried at zero in every scenario, so what falls here is the operating business, not a write-down.

bull.narrative: Water-treatment project wins and food-ingredient and personal-care volumes lift growth two points above the base path, the delivered gross margin holds two points above it as the 2026 selling-price gains stick and the mix moves toward manufacturing, the refinancing is done at a rate near a third lower as the BI rate eases, and the rupiah is five per cent stronger than the deck so the imported cost base helps rather than hurts. Every driver is the bear's, mirrored; the rupiah return is the reciprocal of the bear's depreciation.

sensitivity.title: DCF value per share vs WACC and terminal growth
12-month value vs revenue growth and gross margin

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: Rolled from the filed nine months at the third quarter's run rate: revenue to September 2026 was Rp8,200.8bn, 27.6% above the same period of 2025 and already far beyond the 7%-9% growth the company planned, because volumes and selling prices both rose [F26, F70, F44, F49]. The third quarter alone printed Rp3,090.6bn [F71], so a fourth quarter held flat on it gives Rp11,291.4bn for FY2026E, 28.3% growth. We do not bank the normal fourth-quarter step: in 2025 the fourth quarter (Rp2,383.3bn of the Rp8,799.2bn year) was about 8% above the third (roughly Rp2,200bn, being the nine-month total less the reported first quarter of Rp2,119.4bn [F85] and the second quarter of Rp2,096.6bn) [S0, S13], and we leave that increment to the bull case. From FY2027E the build decelerates to 4%, then 5%, 4.5% and 4%: the company's own 2026 plan is 7%-9% for one year and its revenue CAGR over FY2022-FY2025 was 3.8% [F20, F26, F44, F49], so a return toward mid-single digits is what the record supports once the 2026 price gains annualise; the volume the company names as its 2026 drivers (food ingredients, personal home care, water treatment, basic and specialty chemicals) plus the water-treatment project pipeline is what carries it [S10]. Revenue is not linked to the oil price in the model, so no part of the growth build is attributed to the deck. The terminal rate matches the long-run nominal growth of the reporting currency.

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: Stated at base input costs — FY2025A Brent of US$68.10 and the rupiah at 16,448 — with both cost links applied on top, so that the delivered margin equals the path we intend and no residual link drag sits below it. The path is anchored on what the accounts show: 15.7% in FY2025 (a trough), 17.5% in FY2024, 16.2% in FY2023 and 19.1% in FY2022, a four-year mean near 17.2%, and 18.5% in the nine months to September 2026 as volumes recovered and selling prices improved [S5, S7, F31]. FY2026E delivers 18.2% for the year: the nine months printed 18.5% [F31] and the third quarter 17.3% [F73], so a fourth quarter held at the third quarter's rate gives 18.2%, and that is the delivered figure the input is set to produce, not the nine-month rate extrapolated over twelve months. That is a 2.4pp step up from the FY2025 trough of 15.7%, sourced on the filed nine months; the outer years fade about halfway back toward the four-year mean (17.4% by FY2030E) as the 2026 price gains are competed away, and hold there rather than returning to the trough [S5, S6, S7, S2].

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: share of COGS exposed
assumptions.basis: Calibration, not a company disclosure: 40% of cost of goods sold is treated as Brent-exposed. The cost note splits FY2025 cost of goods sold of Rp7,417.5bn into manufacturing raw materials Rp2,521.5bn, direct labour Rp116.8bn, factory overhead Rp237.9bn and distribution purchases Rp3,741.0bn; the traded and manufactured chemical product is petrochemical-derived, but a distributor's cost is a negotiated principal price rather than a formula Brent price, so half of the product cost is treated as contract-lagged rather than oil-linked [S5]. A larger share would import a commodity-producer cost structure into a distribution business that earns a 13.4% segment gross margin on distribution revenue [F20, F23].

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: pass-through to prices
assumptions.basis: Calibration: 95% of an oil-driven cost move is recovered in selling prices within the year, because the company reprices 1,000-plus products with more than 100 principals and its customer contracts in water treatment and food ingredients are indexed or re-quoted [S7, S2]. The residual 5% is the lag and the competitive constraint in commodity distribution, where INAPLAS members report cheaper imports pressuring petrochemical and plastics prices [S12]. The pair leaves 2% of cost of goods sold exposed, which is consistent with the observed record: Brent rose about two-fifths into FY2026E while the gross margin rose 2.8 percentage points, so the margin move must come from volume, mix and pricing rather than from oil [F31, d.oil.brent].

assumptions.label: Cost link 2: share of COGS imported
assumptions.basis: Calibration, not a company disclosure: 35% of cost of goods sold is treated as priced in dollars. The FY2025 cost note puts distribution purchases at Rp3,741.0bn of Rp7,417.5bn cost of goods sold (50.4%), and the group built its business as an importer and distributor of basic and specialty chemicals, so the bulk of that traded book is imported product [F20, S5]. We take 35% — roughly two-thirds of the traded book — rather than the whole of it, because part of distribution is locally sourced and because the manufacturing raw-material book (Rp2,521.5bn) is largely domestic or already contracted in rupiah [S5, S7].

assumptions.label: Cost link 2: FX pass-through to prices
assumptions.basis: Calibration at 90%: the group reprices more than a thousand product lines with more than a hundred principals, and a rupiah move is passed into the rupiah selling price within a quarter or two [S7, S2]. The residual 10% is the lag and the competitive constraint in commodity distribution, where cheaper imported product is reported to be pressuring prices [S12]. The pair leaves 3.5% of cost of goods sold exposed to the exchange rate, which is the channel through which the currency risk in section 5 now reaches the value rather than sitting in the text alone.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Calibrated on a total-operating-cost basis so that model EBIT equals reported operating income: the LK line "beban usaha" plus net other operating income and expense. In FY2025 that is Rp995.1bn of operating expenses less the Rp26.1bn net other operating income (Rp94.3bn income against Rp68.2bn expense), or 11.01% of revenue [F3, F11, F12]. In the nine months to September 2026 the same basis is Rp873.8bn of operating expenses plus Rp83.9bn net other operating expense, or 11.68% of revenue, because impairments of an associate, of other receivables and of amounts due from related parties were booked [S6, F28]. FY2026E at 11.37% is the filed roll: the third quarter alone ran Rp535.7bn of gross profit less Rp210.0bn of operating income on Rp3,090.6bn of revenue, 10.54%, after the first-half impairments, and holding the fourth quarter at that rate gives 11.37% for the year [F71, F73, F75]. From FY2027E the ratio returns to 11.1% because those impairments are not a recurring annual charge, while the operating leverage shown by nine-month operating expenses growing 16% against revenue growth of 27.6% is kept [S6, F26, F28].

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Fixed-asset depreciation only, taken from the FY2025 note: Rp146,555m allocated across cost of goods sold, services, selling and general expenses, which is 1.67% of revenue [F1]. Right-of-use depreciation of Rp50,162m and intangible amortisation of Rp549m are disclosed separately and excluded from the engine line so that the cash-flow add-back matches the fixed-asset roll-forward [F14, F15]. Held at the FY2025 actual 1.6658% in every forecast year. The operating-expense ratio is struck on reported operating income, which is after depreciation, so the cash-flow add-back has to equal the depreciation embedded in it; the earlier 1.55% holding understated the add-back by about Rp13bn a year and contradicted the same basis, which says capex runs above depreciation and the fixed-asset base grows [F1, F14, F15, S5].

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Held at the last actual: FY2025 acquisitions of fixed assets were Rp215.3bn, 2.45% of revenue, and the cash-flow statement also shows Rp2.2bn of right-of-use additions and Rp2.3bn of investment property [F19, S5]. The annual report's investment table shows Rp138bn of that Rp225bn was assets under construction — warehouses and the subsidiaries' manufacturing facilities in Jakarta, Cikarang, Ciwandan, Tangerang and Surabaya, at completion rates from 2% to 99% — so a substantial part of the FY2025 spend is a project that carries into the forecast rather than one-off maintenance [S10 p.168]. The nine months to September 2026 spent Rp116.6bn, 1.42% of revenue, which is a nine-month rate and not a full-year one; no FY2026 or FY2027 capex budget is disclosed in the annual report or in the quarterly filing [S6, S10]. We therefore model every forecast year at the FY2025 actual 2.45% of revenue, which covers completion of the assets under construction plus the Rp1,852bn fixed-asset base and the routine replacement of distribution vehicles and warehousing. Holding the nine-month rate instead would cut capex intensity by a fifth while revenue grows by a third, which the construction-in- progress balance does not support.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: The working capital cycle was 52 days at 30 September 2026, improved from 56 days a year earlier and 46 days at end-2025, which on the rolled FY2026E revenue of Rp11,291.4bn is roughly 14% of revenue [F33, S2]. The balance sheet confirms it: trade receivables of Rp1,814.5bn plus inventories of Rp1,509.5bn less trade payables of Rp1,692.1bn is Rp1,631.9bn of working capital at 30 September on that revenue base [S6]. Set at 14.2% of revenue and held flat; the mix shift toward manufacturing and water projects keeps inventory days near 61 and receivable days near 60, and no further cycle compression is assumed [S7].

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: Held at the rate the filings actually show being paid, in every forecast year: FY2025 tax expense of Rp61.2bn on pre-tax profit of Rp238.3bn is 25.7% and FY2024 was 30.1% [F9, F7], while the nine months to September 2026 charged Rp140.7bn on Rp416.8bn pre-tax, 33.8% [S6]. FY2026E is 31.6%, the filed nine months at 33.8% plus a fourth quarter at the 26% clean rate; the earlier version dropped to the statutory 26% from FY2027E, which was internally inconsistent because the model carries the non-deductible share of associate losses at a flat run rate for ten years and those losses are what holds the effective rate up in the filing [S6]. A group with a permanent non-deductible loss stream, final tax on certain income and impairments recurring in most years does not reach 26%; the rate is therefore held at the FY2026 blended 31.6% to terminal, which is also the average of the three most recent reported rates (25.7%, 30.1% and 33.8%) [S5, S6, F9, F7].

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 finance costs of Rp131.8bn on opening interest-bearing debt of Rp1,182.5bn is 11.1% [F16, S7]; the nine months to September 2026 cost Rp90.9bn on opening debt of Rp1,349.0bn, 9.0% annualised [S6, F36]. The bonds in issue carry 9.75% to November 2026 and 8.75% to July 2027, and bank lines are shorter and priced off the BI rate [F42, F43]. Set at 9.0%, consistent with the current mix rather than the FY2024 peak.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: FY2025 finance income of Rp3.6bn on opening cash of Rp285.0bn is 1.3%, and nine-month 2026 finance income of Rp2.7bn on cash of Rp276bn is similar [F17, S6]. Indonesian corporate deposit rates on short tenors are well below the policy rate, so 1.2% is held.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: No net new borrowing assumed: the November 2026 bond maturity of Rp135bn and the July 2027 maturity of Rp285.5bn are assumed to be refinanced in place with bank lines or a new shelf issue, so debt is held flat and the 9% cost of debt carries the refinancing rate [F42, F43, S7].

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Carries the associate drag below the operating line at the run rate the filing shows: the share of net losses of associates was Rp52.4bn in the nine months to September 2026 against Rp32.6bn in the same period of 2025, on investments in associates carried at Rp653.3bn [S6 p.7, F66, F37]. Rp52.4bn for three quarters is Rp69.9bn a year, and that annualised rate is held flat in every forecast year: the nine-month comparatives show the loss widening, not narrowing, and the company attributes the associates' result to competitive conditions [S6 p.7, S7]. An earlier version used Rp35bn on the argument that part of the 2026 charge was the associate impairment; that is wrong on the filing's own presentation, because the impairment is booked inside other operating expenses above operating income (S6 p.95, "Penurunan nilai atas investasi pada entitas asosiasi" within Total Other Operating Expenses), so it cannot reduce the below-the-line equity-accounted loss. The two lines are now separate: the impairment sits in opex_pct FY2026E, the share of losses here.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Set at the nine-month 2026 actual: minorities took Rp80.5bn of Rp276.1bn net profit, 29.2%, against Rp21.4bn of Rp141.3bn, 15.1%, in the same nine months of 2025 [S6 p.8]. The mix is shifting toward the manufacturing subsidiaries where the minorities sit, and those are the subsidiaries that led the profit recovery, so there is no sourced reason for the minority share to fall back; FY2025's 15.6% of profit was the trough year when manufacturing profit was depressed [S5, S6]. Held at 29.2% in every forecast year rather than at a judgemental mid-point: minority interest on the balance sheet is Rp314.6bn against parent equity of Rp3,461.7bn [F39, F38].

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: The FY2025 dividend was Rp31 a share against EPS of Rp99, a 31% payout, and cash dividends paid were Rp65.9bn against the prior year's attributable profit of Rp220.4bn [S5, S7]. The board has paid every year through the cycle, including FY2023 and FY2024, and there is no stated policy change, so 30% is held [S10, S9].

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: No change: the buyback programme ended on 21 February 2025 after 90.16m shares, 5.78% of the shares outstanding, were repurchased at an average Rp1,065, and no new programme has been approved [F46, S10].

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: House terminal growth for the rupiah, 4%, anchored to nominal GDP rather than to consumer price inflation. The macro deck carries real GDP growth of 5.29% (gdp_real_id) and CPI of 3.28%, so the nominal GDP growth it implies is about 8.6%; a distributor of imported chemicals grows with nominal industrial demand, which carries real growth as well as price, so nominal GDP is the right anchor and 4% sits well below it and inside the 5% cap. Against the deck's 3.28% CPI the input implies about 0.7% real growth in perpetuity, a deliberately modest real rate for a mature distribution business and the reason we do not take the full nominal rate. The earlier basis said 4% was "below the 3.28% consumer price inflation", which was arithmetically wrong: 4% is above CPI and below nominal GDP [m.gdp_real_id, m.cpi_id, d.macro].

challenges.section: 3. Financial analysis / key inputs: gross_margin, link1_share, link1_pass
challenges.challenge: The Brent link double-charges the 2026 input-cost rise. gross_margin is set at 0.18831, a figure anchored on the 18.5% nine-month actual (S2/F31) earned at the deck's FY2026 Brent of 96.0, and the engine then adds link1_share x (1-link1_pass) x (brent/FY2025A - 1) = 0.4 x 0.05 x 40.9% on top. FY2026E gross margin therefore comes out at 18.17%, 0.66pp and Rp75.1bn of EBIT below the input the analyst chose, and the drag never expires: at the deck's FY2035 Brent of 84.46 it is 0.48% of cogs, Rp65bn. Separately, revenue is not linked at all (params.revenue_mode growth, and the only driver is d.oil.brent into cogs), so the section 2/3 claim that the Brent path drives nominal revenue growth is narrative, not model.
challenges.answer: Rebased every gross_margin input so the delivered margin equals the target: the link is now struck at the FY2025A base (Brent and rupiah), FY2026E delivers 18.17% after the link and FY2035E 17.40%, and the residual drag is gone. The revenue-attribution sentence is removed: revenue is not linked to Brent in this model, so growth decelerates on our own reading of the accounts and the plan, not on the deck. [S5][S2][d.oil.brent]

challenges.challenge: capex_pct is 1.8% of revenue in FY2026E and 1.9% thereafter, against 2.45% in FY2025 (F19, 215.306/8,799.179) and 2.71% in FY2024 (209.44/7,722.38). The only support is the nine-month 1.42%, which is not a full-year rate; S10 p.168 shows Rp138bn of the FY2025 Rp215bn was assets under construction, i.e. projects that carry spend into the forecast. Capex intensity falls 22% while revenue grows 34%. Holding capex at the last actual (2.45%) adds Rp64bn of outflow in FY2027E and Rp89bn by FY2035E, which I make 15-20% of the DCF equity value. The prior round flagged the same 1.8-1.9% and it was not changed.
challenges.answer: capex_pct held at 2.45% of revenue in every forecast year, the FY2025 actual, because no FY2026-27 budget is disclosed and the projects in S10 p.168 carry spend forward; the nine-month 1.42% is a nine-month rate, not a full-year one. [S10][F19]

challenges.challenge: tax_rate is 31.6% in FY2026E and 26.0% from FY2027E to terminal, against 33.8% actually paid in the nine months to September 2026 (Rp140.7bn on PBT of Rp416.8bn, S6) and 30.1% in FY2024 (F10/F8). The model's own permanently non-deductible associate loss of -69.9 a year is precisely what holds the effective rate up, so carrying that loss for ten years and taxing at 26% is internally inconsistent. Each 1pp is about Rp7.6bn of FY2027E FCFF; holding 31.6% costs roughly 9-14% of the DCF equity value.
challenges.answer: tax_rate held at 31.6% in every forecast year, in line with 33.8% in the nine months, 30.1% in FY2024 and 25.7% in FY2025, because the permanently non-deductible associate loss is carried for the whole horizon; the 26% assumption is withdrawn. [S6][S5]

challenges.challenge: NCI is deducted at book, Rp314.6bn (F39), while minorities took 29.2% of nine-month profit (Rp80.5bn of Rp276.1bn, S6) and the model itself assumes 29.2% for every forecast year, i.e. Rp115.8bn of FY2026E group net income of Rp396.6bn. On the model's own group equity value of Rp4,160.7bn that is 10.5x; NCI at book is 2.7x. Capitalising NCI at the model's own multiple deducts about Rp1,215bn instead of Rp314.6bn, a further Rp900bn, roughly Rp615/share or 26% of the v0. Nothing in the report says the minority sits in the lower-return businesses; section 5 says the opposite, that manufacturing (where the minorities sit) led the recovery.
challenges.answer: NCI is now deducted at its capitalised share of the operating equity value rather than at the Rp314.6bn book, and section 4 states the arithmetic, the cost of the change and why book would overstate the parent's claim; section 5 states that the fixed item distorts the tails. [S6][F39]

challenges.challenge: The bridge adds Rp653.3bn of associates less the present value of ten years of losses (Rp416.0bn), leaving +Rp237.3bn. The model's own loss line escalates to -79.1 by FY2035E; capitalised at the 12.42% WACC less the 4% terminal growth that is -Rp940bn, which exceeds the carrying value. The same assumption set that justifies the deduction therefore implies the associates are worth zero, not plus 237.3, and stopping the stream at FY2035 because it is a "run-rate convention" is a bare assertion. The bridge arithmetic also uses a flat 69.9 while the model escalates, so it under-deducts about Rp25bn.
challenges.answer: Associates are now carried at zero in the bridge in every scenario, consistent with a permanent loss stream that capitalises to more than the Rp653.3bn book; the previous plus-signed item is withdrawn. [S6][F37]

challenges.challenge: Section 5 states that "what it does not carry is a write-off of the whole book, which would be worse than our bear", and then leaves it out of the 25% bear. The book is Rp653.3bn, Rp446 per share; a write-off takes the bear from Rp1,117 to about Rp671, below the Rp885 price. As filed, not one of the three scenarios can lose money, so the Rp3,010 weighted value cannot express the downside the report itself names and the distribution is one-sided (bear +26%, bull +516%).
challenges.answer: The bear now loses money: it halves revenue growth, gives back two points of margin, reprices the debt nearly a third higher and weakens the rupiah five per cent, and the bear value sits well below the price. The associate write-down is already pre-booked because the book is carried at zero in every scenario, so the bear shocks the operating business only. [S6][S12]

challenges.challenge: The bridge adds nothing for Rp353.7bn of investments in equity instruments (F41) or Rp452.3bn of investment properties (F67), on the ground that their income "sits inside other operating income". That is wrong for the equities: S6's policy note designates them at fair value through OCI, and S6 shows them rising from Rp217.1bn to Rp353.7bn in nine months, a Rp136.6bn revaluation that by construction never passes through operating income, while their dividends would land in finance income, which the model does not carry (cash_yield applies to cash only). At book that is Rp242/share, 10% of the target, excluded with no source.
challenges.answer: The equity instruments are now added to the bridge at their quoted fair value of Rp353.7bn, citing the S6 policy note that puts the revaluation through OCI and the dividends in finance income; the investment properties stay out, with the S6 note that their rent is booked in other operating income. [S6][F41][F67]

challenges.challenge: The plus/minus 0.05 shock is applied to the growth rate in every forecast year, not to the level, so the tails do not mirror in money. Bull revenue reaches about Rp24,862bn by FY2035E against Rp10,472bn in the bear (2.37x), and the bull contributes Rp1,363 of the Rp3,010 weighted value, 45%. Nine to ten per cent revenue growth for nine years is outside the company's record (revenue CAGR 3.8% FY2022-25, F20-F26) and its own 7-9% one-year plan (S10 p.171). Section 4 describes the bear only as "enough to make FY2027E an outright decline" when the model actually runs -1.0% a year through FY2035E. This is the mirrored-shock asymmetry the card asks reviewers to catch, and it is the largest single contributor to the 179% call.
challenges.answer: Both tails are halved to plus and minus two points on growth and margin, with the same mirrored cost-of-debt and FX shocks, and section 5 discloses that the engine shocks the growth rate rather than the revenue level, the bull's share of the weighted value, and the 30/50/20 probabilities with their reason. [S10][S7][S12]

challenges.challenge: The dividend leg (10% weight) capitalises the forward DPS of Rp57.5 at the peer median trailing yield of 2.64%, giving Rp2,176. That is forward-on-trailing, the pairing the weights_basis and section 4 say they refuse for EV/EBITDA; on trailing DPS of Rp31 the same yield gives Rp1,173. The difference is about Rp100/share of v0, and this is the leg the report calls "the anchor the market is actually using".
challenges.answer: The dividend leg is no longer weighted: forward payout over a trailing peer yield is the same mixed pairing the note refuses for EV/EBITDA, so it is carried as an unweighted cross-check and the blend is 85/15 DCF and EV/EBITDA. [S0][S5]

challenges.challenge: Two claims do not survive their sources. The summary says the nine-month operating margin "nearly doubled" when it went from 4.79% (307.7/6,424.9) to 6.81% (558.8/8,200.8), up 42%; operating income nearly doubled, the margin did not. Second, the Rp885 price and the 52-week high of Rp1,075 rest on S0, which has no archived text, and the high is used to argue the market has already seen the results. Everything else load-bearing that I checked verifies verbatim.
challenges.answer: The margin sentence is corrected: the nine-month step is described as operating income and margin expansion, not a doubling, and the 52-week high is dropped from the argument; the price is cited to the data pack only. [S6][S2][S0]

challenges.section: 4. Valuation / cost of capital and liquidity discount
challenges.challenge: Illiquidity is charged twice on the same name. A 1.0pp COE premium sits inside the 18.37% cost of equity, and a 20.0% discount is then taken off the probability-weighted value (Rp602/share of the 3,010), roughly Rp760/share in total, a third of the 2,360 v0. The prior round accepted a text change on the discount, not a re-derivation, and the assumptions file cites no house rule or limits page that requires both charges together. On top, the beta is relevered on gross debt (Rp1,523/Rp1,296 = 1.175) rather than net debt (0.90), which inflates the levered beta to 1.72 and the COE by about 80bp.
challenges.answer: The illiquidity premium is set to zero, so illiquidity is charged once through the traded-value discount, and section 4 says so; the beta remains relevered on gross interest-bearing debt because the WACC debt weight takes interest-bearing debt while cash is removed in the equity bridge. [S0][S6]

challenges.challenge: Section 5 makes currency the seventh risk and says "the group imports a large share of what it distributes" and that "a sharp move hits one or two quarters of margin", then no scenario carries it: drivers_used in fund record contains only d.oil.brent, there is no FX driver, and the rupiah is already at Rp18,228 against the deck's FY2026E average of Rp17,570 (a 3.6% depreciation). The bear shocks revenue, margin, cost of debt and share count and none of them is the exchange rate, so the stated risk has no number and no value consequence anywhere in the report.
challenges.answer: An FX driver is now in the model: link2 is the rupiah with 35% of cost of goods sold exposed and 90% pass-through, the bear weakens the rupiah five per cent and the bull strengthens it by the reciprocal, and section 5 states the exposure with its source. [S5][d.macro]

challenges.challenge: NCI bridge item is scaled to the DCF pre-minority equity (29.2% x Rp3,552.8bn) but applied unchanged to the EV/EBITDA leg (pre-minority equity Rp2,122.6bn), so that leg deducts 48.9% of it and prints Rp741 against about Rp1,027.
challenges.answer: Fixed at source by removing the defect rather than rescaling it: the engine applies one fixed rupiah bridge to every method, so a per-leg deduction is not expressible. The blend is now the through-cycle DCF alone, where the minority item equals 29.2% less book of that method's own pre-minority equity (Rp1,089.5bn less Rp314.6bn book, item Rp774.9bn); the EV/EBITDA leg is an unweighted cross-check with the basis effect stated in section 4, and the target is re-derived to Rp1,604 [S0, S6].

challenges.challenge: da_pct is 1.55% although its basis cites Rp146.555bn on Rp8,799.179bn, which is 1.67%; FY2026E D&A and the EBITDA line are understated by about Rp13bn.
challenges.answer: da_pct is set to 0.016658 in every forecast year and in the long term, the FY2025 actual of Rp146.555bn on Rp8,799.179bn, and the basis text now says the cash-flow add-back equals the depreciation embedded in reported operating income; the FY2026E D&A and EBITDA lines carry the full charge [S0, S5].

missing_bull_case.note: Two upside arguments remain absent. Rp353.7bn of equity instruments and Rp452.3bn of investment properties are excluded from the bridge at zero on a rationale that fails for the equities (F41 rose 217.1 to 353.7 in nine months through OCI, not through operating income): Rp242/share at book, 10% of the target. And illiquidity is charged twice, 1pp in COE plus the 20% discount, about Rp760/share of a 2,360 v0, with no house rule cited. Credit: the report does quantify the dividend-capacity anchor and net-debt/trough-EBITDA, as the card requires.

missing_bear_case.note: The bear is knowingly incomplete. Section 5 states the associate book write-off is absent because it "would be worse than our bear", and then leaves it out of the 25% bear; the book is Rp446 per share, so the filed bear of 1,117 (still 26% above the price) cannot express a losing outcome. FX is risk 7 in section 5 yet no scenario shocks it and fund record carries no FX driver at all, only d.oil.brent, although a large share of what is distributed is imported.

assumption_realism.note: Revenue is well grounded (9M actual Rp8,200.8bn plus Q4 at Q3's Rp3,090.6bn and 17.3% margin, which reproduces the delivered 18.17% gross margin exactly) and opex is calibrated to reported operating income. The three value drivers that matter are not. Capex is 1.8-1.9% of revenue against 2.45% FY2025 and 2.71% FY2024; tax is 26.0% from FY2027 against 33.8% paid in nine months; and the Brent link charges a 41% 2026 input-cost rise on top of a margin input already earned at 2026 prices. Each is worth 8-20% of the DCF.

evidence_and_citations.note: Spot-checked S2, S5, S6, S7 and S10. Verified verbatim: 9M revenue 8,200.793 and attributable 195.564 and associate loss 52.424 (S6 p.7-8), associates 653.275 and cash 354.828 and NCI 314.572 (S6 p.4), interest-bearing debt 1,523 and the ratio table (S7 p.3-4), capex 215.306 and both bond issues (S5 p.21, 25-26), the 7-9% and 1.5-3% guidance, buyback and LOW 70% (S10 p.11, 28, 171), 27.6% growth and 52-day WCC (S2). Two defects remain: the "nearly doubled" operating margin, and price/52-week high resting on S0, which has no archived text.

valuation_method_fit.note: DCF primary at 75% is the right engine for a CHEMICALS name and the -56% cross-check divergence is confronted, not hidden; the FY2026E re-based multiple at about Rp2,530 is correctly described as within a few per cent of the DCF. The bridge is where the method breaks: NCI is deducted at book 314.6 against 29.2% of earnings, the associate loss stream is truncated at FY2035 although its own perpetuity is negative, and the dividend leg pairs a forward DPS with a trailing peer yield. Each is quantified in the challenges.

bias_and_tone.note: The prose is disciplined and the divergences are stated rather than buried; the rating does not rest on one heroic input (zeroing the bull leaves about Rp1,865, +111%, and doubling the bear probability gives about Rp2,085, +136%). What does not survive is the description of the tails: a -5pp shock to a growth rate applied to every year is not "an outright decline in FY2027E", it is -1.0% a year to FY2035E, and the mirrored +5pp compounds bull revenue to 2.4x the bear. The 45% of the weighted value the bull contributes is a construction artefact as much as a view.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: The CHEMICALS registry is followed: revenue_mode growth, link1 d.oil.brent, and after the prior round the Brent path is described as the deck has it (96.0 in FY2026E, low 76.5 in FY2030, 84.5 by FY2035) and FX and rf are read from the macro deck. The one deck defect is the base node of the link: it is FY2025A Brent of 68.10 while the deck's FY2026E is 96.0, so the 5% unpassed residual is charged against a margin input calibrated at the later price. The same paragraph attributes nominal revenue growth to Brent, but revenue is not linked to it.

conservatism_audit.note: Optimistic departures, all unsourced: tax 26.0% from FY2027 against 33.8% actually paid; capex 1.8-1.9% against 2.45% last actual; NCI deducted at book 314.6 against 115.8 of FY2026E earnings; the associate loss stopped at FY2035; and the div-yield leg's forward DPS. Conservative departures: the Brent link adds 0.66pp of cost in FY2026 (Rp75.1bn of EBIT); the 1pp COE premium sits on gross-debt leverage and a 20% discount on top; and both tails are described more mildly than modelled (the bear runs -1.0% a year, the bull 9-10%). The two sides partly offset, which is why nothing here is FATAL, but the net is a target whose precision the evidence does not support.

calibration.note: The gate reports a 1.99pp FY2025A EBITDA margin gap (actual 6.36%, model 8.35%), just under its 2pp threshold, and it is sourced: the nine-month 2026 EBITDA margin is 8.11% (665/8,200.8, S2) and the 18.5% gross margin is the trough-plus-recovery the model delivers. FY2026E EBITDA of 942.8 is 0.24pp above that run rate. Both flags (extreme_call BLOCK, weights WARN) carry 60-plus-character justifications citing S0/S5/S6/S10, and no drift flag is orphaned.

signoff.notes: Round-1 defect is genuinely fixed at source and the arithmetic verifies. The DCF now carries the whole blend (weight 1.00) and its minority deduction is method-specific: the bridge item of -Rp774.9bn is 29.2% of the DCF's Rp3,731.0bn pre-minority equity (EV 4,545.4 less net debt 1,168.2 plus listed equities 353.7) less the Rp314.6bn book the engine already removes, so the total minority claim is Rp1,089.5bn and no leg carries another leg's scale error. The EV/EBITDA leg is retained only as an unweighted cross-check with the basis effect disclosed line by line in section 4, which is the remedy the return asked for; the target rise from ~1,394 to 1,604 is the arithmetic of that remedy plus the method-card ban on valuing a cyclical on a trailing trough multiple, not a new view. Printed chain re-checks: DCF Rp1,803, base rolled at 17.4% CoE net of Rp58 dps = Rp2,059; scenarios 30/50/20 at Rp316/Rp2,059/Rp4,404 weight to Rp2,005; 20% illiquidity discount gives Rp1,604 and TR 87.8% on Rp885. Facts, lint and engine QC all pass; the single-method blend is disclosed, not silent. Carried editorial FIXes for the next version, neither touching a printed number: section 4 calls 29.2% a share of operating profit where S6 shows net profit, and the associates justification cites a 12.4% WACC against the engine's 12.0%.

bias.note: The round-2 bridge is consistent and sourced both ways: NCI is capitalised at exactly 29.2% of the DCF's Rp3,731.0bn pre-minority equity less the Rp314.6bn book (-774.9, [S6 p.8, F39]), the associates are zeroed because the modelled loss stream capitalises to more than the Rp653.3bn book [F37, F66], and the equity instruments are added at quoted value [F41], all disclosed in section 4. The only conservatism is in the bridge and it is disclosed; revenue growth of 4-5% from FY2027 is sourced to the FY2022-25 CAGR of 3.8% [S10], not felt. No unsourced optimism found.

recomputed.item: FY2026E revenue (9M actual + Q3 held flat)
NCI bridge item (29.2% x pre-minority equity less book)

findings.finding: Section 4's NCI paragraph says the Rp314.6bn non-controlling interest 'took 29.2% of the group's operating profit in the nine months'. The 29.2% is the share of NET profit (Rp80.5bn of Rp276.1bn, [S6 p.8]); 29.2% of operating profit would be Rp163bn and is nowhere used.

The associates bridge item capitalises the loss stream at a '12.4% weighted average cost of capital' while the engine computes 12.0% (model valuation.coc.wacc 11.9679%). The zero-carry conclusion is unchanged either way (perpetual-loss PV about Rp940-990bn against the Rp653.3bn book).

Section 4 says the peer-median EV/EBITDA on FY2026E EBITDA 'produces a value within a tenth of the DCF'. It is +10.5% on EV (Rp5,024bn vs Rp4,545bn) but about +18% per share after the fixed-rupiah bridge (about Rp2,130 vs Rp1,803); name which value is meant.

Three loose ends: qc_justifications carries an orphan 'bridge_nci' entry the engine reports; the report is 8,264 words against the 3,500 results ceiling the lint flags; and the 5 Nov 2026 detik headline 'LTLS Bangun Pabrik Baru' is not archived or addressed while post_bs_review covers debt only - check whether the new plant is material to capex_pct at 2.45%.

flags.message: expected return +88%: name the two or three sourced drivers that produce it and what today's price implies (reverse DCF)
flags.justification: The expected return is produced by three sourced drivers, not by a low discount rate alone. First, earnings power already delivered: nine-month 2026 revenue of Rp8,200.8bn is 27.6% above the same period, operating income of Rp558.8bn is 81.6% higher than the nine-month 2025 figure and the third quarter alone printed Rp3,090.6bn, so the FY2025 base the multiples use is stale [F26, F28, F71, S2]. Second, the market price of Rp885 capitalises that at 3.02 times our FY2026E EBITDA of Rp956.4bn and 0.40 times our FY2026E projected parent equity, against a peer median of 5.25 times trailing EBITDA [S0]. Both multiples are the engine's own: the 3.02x is fund record multiples.FY2026E.ev_ebitda and the 5.25x is the peer median the engine computes from the CHEMICALS data packs, not a figure from a filing [S0]. Third, the balance sheet carries non-operating value the earnings multiple ignores: associates at Rp653.3bn on the book, equity instruments at Rp353.7bn at quoted price and investment properties at Rp452.3bn [F37, F41, F67, S6]. The equity bridge carries the associates at zero (their operating losses are modelled inside the group, so adding the book would double count them) and the listed equity instruments at their quoted value [F37, F41]; the investment properties stay out because their rental income already sits inside the EBITDA we capitalise (section 4). The 20% illiquidity discount and the small free float are carried into the target [S0, S10].

flags.message: method weights differ from the industry default {'dcf_fcff': 0.6, 'ev_ebitda': 0.25, 'pe': 0.15}
flags.justification: The weights are re-stated from the CHEMICALS default 60/25/15 to 100% DCF for two reasons that point the same way. First, the earnings multiples can only read the data pack's trailing series, which falls back to FY2025, the trough year, and the peer multiples are themselves trailing [S0, S5], so the through-cycle DCF carries the value per VAL_COMMODITY_CYCLICAL step 1. Second, the Sector Lead's round-2 finding: the engine applies one fixed rupiah bridge to every method, and a minority claim capitalised on the DCF's own pre-minority equity deducts 48.9% rather than 29.2% of the EV/EBITDA leg's much smaller equity base, printing a floor about Rp285 below what that leg implies. With one bridge item and two equity bases the defect cannot be calibrated away, so the leg whose deduction is exact is the leg that values the company; the multiple is reported as a cross-check in section 4, not as a weighted method [S0, S6].
